lectures.title: Letting Flutter do the Work with TextEditingController

cues.en: So reacting to every key press
and updating and storing the current value of the text field
in some variable
is one way of handling and storing the user input.
But of course, it can be a bit cumbersome
to manually store all the input
for all the text fields
that might make up your user interface.
And that's why Flutter gives you a convenient alternative.
Nonetheless, it's also important
to know about this approach
because it's also a valid approach
that you might see in many projects you're working on.
But the alternative you get
does not require you to add this function
and this extra storage variable.
Instead, we'll add another property,
which can be a final property now
to this NewExpenseState class.
And this is a property
that could be called titleController.
Now, the name might be a bit strange,
and of course it is up to you,
but I chose titleController here
because the value which will be stored in this property
will be an object that is created
with help of the built-in TextEditingController class,
which is a class provided by Flutter.
Now, this creates an object
that's optimized for handling user input, you could say,
an object that can be passed as a value to text field
to let flutter do all the heavy lifting
of storing the entered value and so on.
Now, when using TextEditingController,
there's one thing that's really important
to keep in mind though.
When you create a TextEditingController here,
you also have to tell Flutter to delete that controller
when the widget is not needed anymore,
so for example, when the modal overlay is closed,
because otherwise this TextEditingController
which you create here
would live on in memory
even though the widget is not visible anymore.
That's why when using TextEditingController,
you should also always add the special dispose method
to your state class here.
So a method called dispose,
which returns nothing,
and calls super.dispose.
And before calling super.dispose,
you should reach out to your controller,
and on that controller,
call the dispose method,
so that you tell Flutter
that this controller is not needed anymore.
Otherwise it will not be deleted,
and ultimately your device memory
might be taken up by all these unnecessary controllers,
and that could cause your app to crash.
So therefore, you should always dispose
of these TextEditingControllers
you might be creating.
But what's the idea behind this controller now?
Well, with it created,
you can go to your text field
and get rid of this onChanged parameter,
which you now don't need anymore.
And instead you can set a controller parameter.

So if you have multiple fields,

And you can now also use this titleController here

Here, you can access your titleController,
